The test image shows a microscope view of soybean stem tissue with numerous tiny black specks (microsclerotia) scattered throughout pale, fibrous stem tissue — the classic "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance.

**Key observations:**
- Microscope/close-up view of stem interior
- Pale/tan fibrous tissue background
- Countless small black dots (microsclerotia) scattered throughout the tissue
- Not in linear rows (ruling out Diaporthe)
- Not large acervuli with setae (ruling out Anthracnose)
- No white mycelium or large sclerotia (ruling out White Mold)
- No brown pith discoloration pattern (ruling out Brown Stem Rot)

This perfectly matches **Charcoal Rot**: "small black specks (microsclerotia) beneath the epidermis giving a charcoal-sprinkled appearance" and "gray hyphae and microsclerotia streaking visible internally."
